answers.gripWhy: You give up the consul's sole power over the papers.

answers.text: Refuse; Caesar's acts are law, and you guard them.
answers.sub: You keep the papers and the June law's power.

reasons.cpt: Caesar's acts stand untouched: our provinces and priesthoods safe.
reasons.gal: My decree stands, and my bond is honoured.
reasons.oct: My father's papers stay in your house, not mine.
reasons.sen: Forged decrees, and the consul refuses all scrutiny.
reasons.lbr: He hides behind a dead tyrant's notebooks.

answers.gripWhy: You rule on Caesar's acts alone, over the Senate.

answers.text: Void every act not posted before the Ides.
answers.sub: Only what Caesar published while alive remains law.

reasons.lbr: The dead tyrant stops legislating from his tomb.
reasons.sen: An end to forgeries; the Senate breathes again.
reasons.cpt: Grants Caesar promised us torn up by his own consul.
reasons.gal: Armenia's decree gone, and my ten million wasted.
reasons.plb: Caesar's promised gifts to us may die too.

situations.title: The Euphrates Question

carrier.name: Titus Annaeus Celer
carrier.role: Junior military tribune back from Syria

situations.question: Parthia's envoys wait. Will you march east, buy peace, or leave Syria?
situations.body: Caesar's sixteen legions and 10,000 horse for the Parthian war are standing down. Six legions wait in Macedonia. In Syria, Pompeian rebels hold Apamea, and Parthian riders have been seen with them. Orodes's envoys ask whether Rome still means war. Dolabella wants Syria for himself.

answers.text: Keep Caesar's war: the legions march east.
answers.sub: Caesar's campaign goes on under your eagles, vengeance for Carrhae.

reasons.cpt: Caesar's war, Caesar's legions: plunder and glory for us.
reasons.egy: Roman legions in the East keep the Liberators off my throne.
reasons.par: Caesar's avenger at the Euphrates: the war we feared.
reasons.oct: You take my father's campaign and his soldiers.
reasons.eqt: War on the Euphrates halts the tribute of Asia.

answers.text: Send envoys; fix peace on the Euphrates by treaty.
answers.sub: A senatorial embassy, gifts exchanged, the old frontier confirmed.

reasons.par: The war cancelled and Rome's generals busy with each other.
reasons.sen: Treaties by embassy: foreign policy back in the Curia.
reasons.eqt: Peace keeps the Asian tax contracts flowing.
reasons.gal: Peace on the Euphrates keeps armies off Anatolia's roads.
reasons.cpt: Caesar's war sold off for a treaty.
reasons.egy: Peace with Parthia leaves Egypt's Roman friends weaker.

answers.text: Bring the legions home and settle them on land.
answers.sub: Discharges and allotments in Italy instead of a desert war.

reasons.plb: Land in Italy, not graves in Mesopotamia.
reasons.par: No legions marching east: the Euphrates stays quiet.
reasons.cpt: Veterans settled on land remember who gave it.
reasons.eqt: New colonies mean surveys of our Italian estates.
reasons.egy: An empty Syria is an open road to Cassius.

situations.title: Answer to Cicero
situations.question: Cicero has spoken against you. How will you answer him?
situations.body: Second of September. Cicero, returned to Rome, stood in the Senate and attacked your use of Caesar's papers. He offered you friendship if you govern by the laws. You were at Tibur. The speech is already copied and passed hand to hand.

answers.text: Offer Cicero a share in the settlement.
answers.sub: Consult him on the acts; his friends gain posts.

reasons.sen: The first consular consulted: auctoritas restored.
reasons.eqt: Atticus's friend reconciled with the consul: peace is good business.
reasons.lbr: Cicero at the table speaks for the amnesty.
reasons.cpt: Sharing power with the man who praised the murderers.
reasons.oct: The old orator was mine to win, not yours.

answers.gripWhy: You bring your fiercest critic into council.

answers.text: Send the guild men to his Palatine house.
answers.sub: A crowd at his door, torches, and his speeches stop.

reasons.plb: The old Pompeian learns the street's opinion of him.
reasons.cpt: Cicero silenced is one less voice for the assassins.
reasons.sen: A consular besieged at home, like Clodius's days.
reasons.eqt: Mobs at senators' doors; next they come for ours.
reasons.lbr: Free speech answered with torches: the tyranny returns.

answers.gripWhy: A crowd besieges a consular's house to silence him.

answers.text: Answer him in the Senate, speech for speech.
answers.sub: Free debate: you reply at length on 19 September.

reasons.sen: The quarrel kept inside the Curia, where it belongs.
reasons.lbr: Even the consul must argue in a free Senate.
reasons.plb: Speeches, while Cicero spits on Caesar's memory.
reasons.cpt: Caesar's consul debating the assassins' friend like an equal.
reasons.oct: Debating Cicero, you forget my father's murderers.

answers.gripWhy: You let the quarrel be fought with words, freely.

situations.title: The Praetors' Edict

carrier.name: Quintus Pedanius Alba
carrier.role: Courier from the Bay of Naples

situations.question: Brutus and Cassius say they will leave Italy. Will you let them go?
situations.body: Brutus and Cassius have sent you an edict. They protest threats to their lives and say they will leave Italy rather than cause a war. Merchants from Brundisium report ships hired. Your agents say they mean Macedonia and Syria, with their treasuries and legions.

answers.text: Let them sail freely, under the amnesty.
answers.sub: Your edict guarantees their safety; no ship is stopped.

reasons.lbr: Our lives guaranteed and our road open.
reasons.sen: The amnesty of Tellus honoured, as the Senate swore.
reasons.par: Friends of Parthia arrive in Syria with full hands.
reasons.egy: The assassins sail toward my borders, unhindered.
reasons.cpt: Caesar's murderers sail off to raise armies against us.
reasons.plb: The consul waves Caesar's killers off with a blessing.

answers.gripWhy: You let the Liberators go free, unwatched, under the amnesty.

answers.text: Give them Crete and Cyrene by Senate decree.
answers.sub: Minor provinces, lawfully allotted, far from the legions of the East.

reasons.sen: Provinces by decree and by lot: the Senate decides again.
reasons.eqt: A lawful settlement keeps Asia's taxes clear of armies.
reasons.lbr: Crete and Cyrene: sheep and rocks for the liberators of Rome.
reasons.cpt: Provinces for assassins, granted by Caesar's own consul.
reasons.oct: My father's murderers rewarded with governorships.

situations.title: Bounty at Brundisium
situations.question: The legions jeer your hundred denarii. What will you do with them?
situations.body: Four Macedonian legions have landed at Brundisium. You offered 100 denarii a man; they laughed on parade. Octavian's agents move through the camp promising 500 and the name of Caesar. Pamphlets are found in the tents. The Martia's centurions will not meet your eye.

answers.text: Seize the ringleaders and execute them before the ranks.
answers.sub: Centurions named by lot die; the rest swear to you.

reasons.cpt: Mutiny punished in the old way; the eagles obey again.
reasons.eqt: Discipline is cheaper than a fivefold donative.
reasons.oct: You kill my father's soldiers; I will avenge them.
reasons.sen: A consul killing citizens in camp without trial.
reasons.plb: Caesar's veterans killed by Caesar's own consul.

answers.gripWhy: Executions in the ranks; fear holds the camp.

answers.text: Promise each man land and a share of colonies.
answers.sub: Allotments in Italy after the campaign, by the board of seven.

reasons.cpt: Land after victory: the old promise that binds veterans.
reasons.eqt: More colonies, more of our Italian estates surveyed.
reasons.sen: The agrarian board grows into a private army's paymaster.
reasons.oct: You match my offer with land; my silver buys less.
reasons.plb: Veterans take the land promised to the city's poor.

answers.text: Hold them to their oath and the standard pay.
answers.sub: Arrears paid in full; no bounty, no killing, the sacramentum read.

reasons.sen: Soldiers bound by oath, not bought: the old discipline.
reasons.eqt: No bidding war for the legions; the Treasury survives.
reasons.lbr: An army bound to law, not to one man's purse.
reasons.cpt: Oaths without silver won't hold Caesar's veterans; we lose them.

situations.title: The Heir Marches
situations.question: Octavian marches on Rome with paid veterans. What will you do about him?
situations.body: Octavian has bought some 3,000 of Caesar's veterans in Campania at 500 denarii a man. He marches up the Via Appia to speak against you in the Forum. He is nineteen and holds no office. A tribune has promised him the Rostra.

answers.text: Ask the Senate to declare him a public enemy.
answers.sub: Convene the Curia: a private army is treason by any law.

reasons.lbr: The young avenger outlawed: one danger less for us.
reasons.eqt: Private armies bought with silver must be stopped.
reasons.sen: You ask us to outlaw the one army that checks you.
reasons.oct: Caesar's son named an enemy by Caesar's consul.
reasons.cpt: Outlawing Caesar's heir splits the party in two.

answers.gripWhy: You seek outlawry against a citizen without trial.

answers.text: Treat with him as Caesar's son; share the vengeance.
answers.sub: Confirm his adoption, pay the bequest, join forces against the assassins.

reasons.oct: My adoption confirmed, my father's money and my place.
reasons.plb: The 300 sesterces at last, and Caesar's men united.
reasons.cpt: No Caesarian fights Caesarian: the veterans breathe.
reasons.lbr: Two Caesars joined means our heads on the Rostra.
reasons.sen: The Caesarians unite, and the Senate stands alone.

answers.text: Call a contio and pay the bequest yourself.
answers.sub: You give the plebs Caesar's 300 sesterces before the boy can.

reasons.plb: Silver in our hands and Caesar's will honoured.
reasons.cpt: The plebs back the consul; the boy's march fails.
reasons.oct: You pay my father's bequest to steal my people.
reasons.sen: Buying the Forum with Caesar's treasury, again.
reasons.eqt: Millions poured out to the mob while loans go unpaid.

situations.title: Swords in the Forum

carrier.name: Publius Numitorius
carrier.role: Attendant of a tribune of the plebs

situations.question: The tribunes protest your armed guard. Will you keep the soldiers in the city?
situations.body: Six thousand veterans camp around your house and line the Forum on Senate days. Ituraean archers stand on the Capitol steps. The tribunes say no armed men may stand inside the pomerium. Shopkeepers in the Argiletum close early. The crowd is quiet, and watching.

answers.text: Keep the guard; the consul's person must be safe.
answers.sub: Veterans stay in the Forum on every Senate day.

reasons.cpt: Caesar walked without guards and died; you will not.
reasons.sen: Senators vote with swords at their backs: no free Curia.
reasons.lbr: A tyrant's bodyguard, exactly as we foresaw.
reasons.plb: Soldiers on our streets, as if the city were conquered.
reasons.eqt: Armed men in the Forum frighten every creditor.

answers.gripWhy: Armed men stand inside the pomerium by your order.

answers.text: Disband the guard; no arms inside the pomerium.
answers.sub: You walk the Forum with lictors only, as custom demands.

reasons.sen: The Senate meets without swords at the door again.
reasons.lbr: Even the consul bows to the old law of the pomerium.
reasons.eqt: A city without soldiers is good for trade.
reasons.plb: The Forum belongs to the people again, not the soldiers.
reasons.cpt: Caesar's consul strips himself bare before his enemies.

answers.gripWhy: Soldiers leave the city; the Forum is open again.

situations.title: Alba Fucens
situations.question: Two legions have gone to Octavian. How will you hold the rest?
situations.body: The Legio Martia marched to Alba Fucens and shut its gates on you. The Fourth followed under its quaestor. Octavian promised them 500 denarii and Caesar's name. The Second and the Thirty-Fifth still hold. The Alaudae are within call.

answers.text: March north with the loyal Second and Thirty-Fifth.
answers.sub: Your loyal legions go with you to Cisalpine Gaul.

reasons.cpt: A general with legions marching: Caesar's way, at last.
reasons.sen: The consul leaves Rome to make war on Decimus.
reasons.lbr: Decimus at Mutina is the next to be hunted.
reasons.plb: Our consul rides north and leaves the city to the boy.
reasons.eqt: War in Cisalpine Gaul closes the northern markets.

answers.gripWhy: You take the army out to settle Gaul by force.

answers.text: Recruit the city's poor to fill the ranks.
answers.sub: Volunteers from the Subura enrolled for pay and land.

reasons.plb: Pay, bread and a sword for the Subura's young men.
reasons.cpt: Raw city boys in place of Caesar's veterans.
reasons.sen: Arming the rabble of Rome, like Catiline.
reasons.eqt: An armed mob drawn from the debtors' streets.

answers.gripWhy: Armed recruits drill in the city's own streets.

answers.text: Let them go; you keep no legions in Italy.
answers.sub: The deserters are released; you go north with lictors only.

reasons.sen: No army in Italy against our decree: the red line kept.
reasons.lbr: A consul without legions is no tyrant.
reasons.oct: The legions are mine, and you did not fight me.
reasons.eqt: No civil war means debts paid and tribute flowing.
reasons.cpt: You throw away Caesar's legions without a blow.
reasons.plb: Who guards Caesar's acts now? The boy?

answers.gripWhy: You give up your army and the soldiers' oath.

situations.title: The Night Allotment
situations.question: Consul, the Senate sits by lamplight. How will you hand out the provinces?
situations.body: It is the night of 28 November. The Martia and the Fourth have gone to Octavian. You ride for Gaul at dawn. Macedonia, Africa and Crete wait for praetors. Your brother Gaius is praetor this year. The senators sit few and frightened.

answers.text: Leave the provinces to the lot, as custom requires
answers.sub: The urn decides; the Senate sees a lawful consul.

reasons.sen: The lot by our custom: a consul who still respects us.
reasons.cpt: A blind urn may hand Macedonia to a Senate man.
reasons.plb: No reward for the tribunes who carried his laws.
reasons.eqt: Lawful allotment calms the tax companies of Macedonia.
reasons.lbr: A fair lot might leave Macedonia open to Brutus.

answers.gripWhy: The Senate allots freely, without your soldiers at the door.

answers.text: Give Macedonia to your brother Gaius
answers.sub: Its legions and treasury stay in the family's hands.

reasons.cpt: A Caesarian holds the road east against the assassins.
reasons.sen: A consul's brother by decree at night: Caesar's way again.
reasons.lbr: Macedonia was to be Brutus's refuge; now it is shut.
reasons.oct: The consul's family grows while Caesar's son gets nothing.
reasons.egy: A Caesarian across the sea from Egypt suits the queen.

answers.gripWhy: Provinces dealt by night to kin, with veterans at the doors.

answers.text: Reward the tribunes' friends with Africa and Crete
answers.sub: The men who carried the land law get rich commands.

reasons.plb: Our tribunes' allies rewarded: the people's laws are safe.
reasons.sen: Provinces as wages for demagogues, not by lot.
reasons.eqt: Crete and Africa farmed by your friends, not by us.
reasons.cpt: Friends rewarded keep their loyalty to the Caesarian cause.
reasons.lbr: More of the consul's creatures holding armies and treasuries.

situations.title: Decimus Shuts Mutina

carrier.name: Lucius Seius Pudens
carrier.role: Senior centurion of the Second Legion

situations.question: Decimus holds Mutina against you. Will you storm it, starve it, or bargain?
situations.body: Decimus Brutus has posted his edict: he holds Cisalpine Gaul for the Senate, not for you. He has shut his legions inside Mutina with salted cattle and grain. Your law gave you this province. The walls are strong; winter has come to the Po.

answers.text: Storm the walls before Hirtius can march
answers.sub: Your veterans take Mutina by assault, at a heavy price.

reasons.cpt: Caesar's assassin dragged from his walls: vengeance at last.
reasons.lbr: One of us faces the sword for the Ides.
reasons.sen: A proconsul attacking the Senate's governor: open war.
reasons.oct: Your victory at Mutina leaves no army needing the heir.
reasons.plb: An assassin besieged: the Forum cheers the avenger.

answers.gripWhy: Roman legions storm a Roman town held by the Senate's man.

answers.text: Starve him out behind lawful siege lines
answers.sub: Ring Mutina with ditches; insist the province is yours by law.

reasons.sen: Lawful words around an unlawful siege still offend us.
reasons.eqt: A slow siege spares the Po valley's estates and towns.
reasons.lbr: Hunger is slower than the sword, but it is the sword.
reasons.cpt: Patience wins the province without bleeding Caesar's veterans.
reasons.oct: Months of siege give the heir time to arm.

answers.gripWhy: A blockade by your army, though dressed in the law.

answers.text: Offer Decimus a safe road to Macedonia
answers.sub: He keeps his life and honour; you take Gaul unbloodied.

reasons.lbr: Decimus lives and goes east to join Brutus.
reasons.cpt: A Caesarian army lets Caesar's betrayer walk free.
reasons.oct: My father's murderer walks away with his legions.
reasons.sen: A bloodless end honours the Senate's man.
reasons.par: Another Liberator army in the East keeps Rome divided.

answers.gripWhy: You trade the siege for terms and a free road.

situations.title: Ventidius in Picenum
situations.question: Ventidius can raise two legions. Will you pay them with Picene land?
situations.body: Ventidius, once a mule-dealer, now a Caesarian general, stands ready in Picenum. Caesar's veterans there will answer his call. They want land, not promises. Some Picene towns have shut their gates to your agents. Their equites watch from their farms.

answers.text: Pay them with the towns that refuse you
answers.sub: Defiant towns forfeit land and goods to the new legions.

reasons.cpt: Two veteran legions, paid by enemies, under Caesarian standards.
reasons.oct: Picenum's veterans go to the consul instead of me.
reasons.eqt: Confiscations in Italy: the proscriptions of Sulla return.
reasons.sen: Roman towns plundered to pay a consul's private army.
reasons.plb: Soldiers paid by the rich towns, not by grain money.

answers.gripWhy: Citizens' land seized at swordpoint to pay your soldiers.

answers.text: Settle them under your brother's land law
answers.sub: Lucius's board of seven gives public land to veterans and poor.

reasons.plb: Land for the poor citizens, not only for soldiers.
reasons.cpt: Veterans settled are veterans who will fight again.
reasons.eqt: Public land we lease is taken for allotments.
reasons.sen: Your brother's board carves Italy without the Senate's leave.
reasons.oct: Veterans settled by Antonius forget the heir's silver.

situations.title: Murder at Smyrna

carrier.name: Philotas
carrier.role: Freedman courier of the Asian tax companies

situations.question: Dolabella has killed Trebonius. Will you disown him or stand by him?
situations.body: Dolabella entered Smyrna by night and seized Trebonius, proconsul of Asia. He put him to death after two days of questioning. Trebonius kept you talking outside the Curia on the Ides. The Senate is moving to name Dolabella a public enemy. He marches for Syria.

answers.text: Disown him: no magistrate may murder a proconsul
answers.sub: You join the Senate's vote that brands Dolabella an enemy.

reasons.lbr: Trebonius avenged in law, even by the proconsul's own mouth.
reasons.cpt: A Caesarian disowns a Caesarian over an assassin's death.
reasons.sen: You stand with the Senate against a murderer: good.
reasons.egy: Dolabella was the queen's best Roman hope in Syria.
reasons.eqt: Asia's tax chests need a lawful governor, not a brigand.

answers.text: Stand by Dolabella as master of the East
answers.sub: Your colleague holds Syria's legions and your eastern flank.

reasons.cpt: One Caesarian holds the East while another holds Gaul.
reasons.egy: A Caesarian in Syria shields Egypt from Cassius.
reasons.lbr: You embrace the butcher of Trebonius: the amnesty is dead.
reasons.sen: You defend the murder of a proconsul; we answer with war.
reasons.par: A Caesarian army on the Euphrates is what we fear.

answers.gripWhy: You bless a governor's murder as an act of state.

situations.title: The Senate's Embassy
situations.question: The consulars order you out of Gaul. Will you obey, refuse, or bargain?
situations.body: Piso and Servius Sulpicius reach your camp before Mutina. The old jurist is sick from the winter road. The Senate's decree is plain: lift the siege, quit Cisalpine Gaul, stay 200 miles from Rome. Octavian now sits in the Senate with imperium.

answers.text: Obey: lift the siege and leave the province
answers.sub: You keep your life and rank; Decimus keeps Gaul.

reasons.sen: The Senate's decree obeyed by a proconsul: authority restored.
reasons.lbr: Decimus is freed and the Liberators' cause lives.
reasons.cpt: You hand Caesar's province to his murderer without a fight.
reasons.plb: The people's law giving you Gaul is torn up by senators.
reasons.oct: With no war, the Senate no longer needs the heir's army.

answers.gripWhy: You lay down the sword at the Senate's word.

answers.text: Offer terms: disarm only if Brutus and Cassius disarm
answers.sub: Neither you nor the Liberators keep armies against the laws.

reasons.lbr: Brutus and Cassius told to give up the East they won.
reasons.sen: Terms at least: a door left open to peace.
reasons.cpt: Bargaining with assassins' armies instead of crushing them.
reasons.oct: Peace among the old men leaves the heir with nothing.
reasons.par: Disarmed Roman armies leave the Euphrates quiet.

answers.gripWhy: You put your command up for bargaining in the open.

answers.text: Refuse: the tribes gave you Gaul, not the Senate
answers.sub: You hold the province by the people's vote of June.

reasons.plb: Our vote stands above their decree. Good.
reasons.cpt: Caesar's men keep Gaul and their swords.
reasons.sen: A proconsul defies our embassy: the ultimate decree must follow.
reasons.eqt: War in the Po valley stops rents and loans.
reasons.lbr: Decimus stays starving in Mutina.

answers.gripWhy: You defy the Senate's envoys with your legions behind you.

situations.title: Seventeen Legions Wait
situations.question: Lepidus, Plancus and Pollio wait. What will you write to win them?
situations.body: Lepidus holds Narbonensis and Nearer Spain. Plancus holds Gallia Comata. Pollio holds Further Spain. Between them stand seventeen legions. Each writes to Cicero of his love for the Republic. Each writes to you of old friendship. None has yet moved.

answers.text: Write as Caesar's officer: avenge him together
answers.sub: Call on their oath to Caesar and their veterans' memory.

reasons.cpt: Caesar's lieutenants called to their old cause, under one banner.
reasons.oct: The proconsul claims Caesar's legions, my inheritance.
reasons.sen: The western armies summoned to a war of vengeance.
reasons.lbr: Seventeen legions sworn to vengeance against us.
reasons.plb: Caesar's soldiers united: the avengers grow stronger.

answers.text: Promise their soldiers land under the people's law
answers.sub: Speak over the generals' heads to the rank and file.

reasons.plb: Soldiers and people bound together under the people's laws.
reasons.cpt: Talking to our soldiers over our heads breaks command.
reasons.eqt: More land promised means more estates surveyed and taken.
reasons.oct: My agents' offers to the same soldiers now look meagre.
reasons.sen: Legions courted with land like a Gracchus's mob.

answers.text: Remind them you abolished the dictatorship forever
answers.sub: Your law of April proves you seek no crown.

reasons.sen: A fair reminder: the consul who ended the dictatorship.
reasons.lbr: If you mean it, there is no tyrant to fight.
reasons.cpt: Caesar's generals want provinces, not the speeches of philosophers.
reasons.oct: You disclaim Caesar's power; I gladly claim it.
reasons.plb: The crowd wants an avenger, not a lawyer's pledge.

answers.gripWhy: You bind your own hand by law before the armies.

situations.title: The Ultimate Decree

carrier.name: Gaius Petronius Sura
carrier.role: Secretary to your friends in the Senate

situations.question: Your enemies passed the ultimate decree. Will you fight it, quit, or rouse Rome?
situations.body: On 2 February the Senate declared a tumultus. Citizens wear the military cloak in the streets. The ultimate decree charges Hirtius, Pansa and Octavian to see the state come to no harm. Your friends still hold seats in the Curia. They wait for your word.

answers.text: Stay in the Curia and press for peace terms
answers.sub: Your friends argue for a new embassy and lawful terms.

reasons.sen: Your friends debate by the rules; the Curia still governs.
reasons.eqt: Talk in the Curia means loans and rents keep flowing.
reasons.oct: Peace talks threaten the war that makes the heir needed.
reasons.cpt: Debate while the legions march is weakness.
reasons.plb: Senators bargaining over the people's heads again.

answers.gripWhy: Your men argue in the open Curia, not in camp.

answers.text: Order your friends out: let the legions decide
answers.sub: Your men leave Rome for your camp; only the sword remains.

reasons.cpt: Caesar's men stop pleading with senators and draw swords.
reasons.sen: The proconsul's friends abandon the Curia: open war is declared.
reasons.eqt: Open war in Italy: every debt is now at risk.
reasons.oct: Every senator left in Rome is now the heir's.
reasons.lbr: A Caesarian army with no voice left but the sword.

answers.gripWhy: You trade the Curia's debate for the soldiers' oath.

answers.text: Rouse the tribes against the decree
answers.sub: Your brother's friends call contiones: the people versus the ultimate decree.

reasons.plb: The ultimate decree killed the Gracchi; we remember.
reasons.sen: Mobs against the Senate's decree, as in Clodius's days.
reasons.eqt: Street fighting in Rome empties the banks of the Forum.
reasons.oct: The crowd I bought turns to Antonius's men.
reasons.cpt: The city stirs for Caesar's party behind the consuls' backs.

answers.gripWhy: You call the crowd to the Forum, not the soldiers.

situations.title: Sextus Pompeius's Price
situations.question: Sextus Pompeius commands the Senate's fleet. What will you give him?
situations.body: The Senate has made Pompey's son prefect of the fleet and the sea coasts. His ships came out of Spain with Pompeian exiles aboard. His envoy names a price: his father's house on the Carinae and his estates. You live in that house now.

answers.text: Restore his father's estates and the exiles' rights
answers.sub: Pompey's son and his exiles return as free citizens.

reasons.lbr: Pompeian exiles freed: the old Republic gathers its sons.
reasons.cpt: Caesar's enemies paid with Caesar's spoils.
reasons.sen: The fleet kept from war by a lawful restitution.
reasons.oct: Pompey's son restored: a rival name to Caesar's.
reasons.eqt: Estates our members bought at auction now in question.

answers.gripWhy: You pardon and restore men Caesar's victory had outlawed.

answers.text: Pay him to keep the grain ships sailing
answers.sub: Silver for Sextus; Sicily's grain still reaches the Tiber.

reasons.plb: Grain keeps coming: the people eat whatever the war.
reasons.eqt: Our silver buys peace with a pirate.
reasons.sen: The proconsul bargains with the Senate's own admiral.
reasons.egy: With Sextus quiet, Egypt's grain can sail without fear.
reasons.cpt: Silver to a Pompeian while our soldiers wait for pay.

situations.title: Pansa on the Aemilian Road
situations.question: Pansa's recruits march up the Via Aemilia. Will you strike them or hold?
situations.body: Pansa leads four legions of new recruits from Rome. Hirtius and Octavian wait near Forum Cornelii. Inside Mutina, Decimus's men eat their horses. Your veterans of the Second and Thirty-Fifth know the road at Forum Gallorum. The marshes there hide an army.

answers.text: Strike Pansa in the marshes before he joins Hirtius
answers.sub: Your veterans ambush the recruits on the road.

reasons.cpt: Caesar's veterans against boys: a soldier's battle, a soldier's win.
reasons.sen: A proconsul attacks a consul of Rome on the march.
reasons.oct: The heir's allies cut down before he can join them.
reasons.plb: Sons of Rome's streets fall to Roman veterans.
reasons.lbr: Decimus's relief delayed while his men eat their horses.

answers.gripWhy: You turn the legions on a sitting consul.

answers.text: Hold the siege lines and keep the camps fortified
answers.sub: Let them come to you; Decimus surrenders first.

reasons.cpt: Waiting lets three armies join against us.
reasons.lbr: Mutina starves another month behind your ditches.
reasons.eqt: No pitched battle yet: the Po valley may still be spared.
reasons.sen: No consul attacked: room yet for a decree of peace.
reasons.oct: Time lets the heir's legions join the consuls.

answers.text: Send word to the recruits: land for deserters
answers.sub: Your agents promise allotments to any recruit who crosses over.

reasons.plb: Plebeian recruits offered land instead of a grave.
reasons.sen: The consul's levies bribed to desert their consul.
reasons.eqt: More land promised from whose estates? Ours.
reasons.oct: The recruits I marched with may be bought away.
reasons.cpt: Fewer enemies on the road means fewer veterans lost.

callbacks.title: Acts No One Saw

carrier.name: Aulus Fannius Celer
carrier.role: Clerk at the Temple of Saturn treasury

callbacks.question: Consul, will you let the Senate judge the acts you found, or the tribes?
callbacks.body: In March you drew new decrees from Caesar's notebooks. Bronze tablets on the Capitol now free whole cities from tribute and restore exiles. Senators say no one saw Caesar sign them. Atticus reports the publicani losing the revenues of Crete and Sicily.

answers.text: Submit the disputed acts to a board of consulars.
answers.sub: The Senate's men decide which decrees stand; some are struck.

reasons.sen: The consulars at last judge what Caesar truly signed.
reasons.eqt: Struck exemptions return the revenues to the companies.
reasons.lbr: The tyrant's forged hand is restrained.
reasons.cpt: Caesar's gifts to his friends are taken back.
reasons.gal: The Armenian decree may be struck and the bond wasted.

answers.text: Have the tribes confirm every act by law.
answers.sub: The assembly votes Caesar's acts law, over the Senate's head.

reasons.plb: The tribes, not the Senate, make Caesar's acts law.
reasons.cpt: Every act stands; every friend keeps his reward.
reasons.gal: The decree for Armenia becomes Roman law.
reasons.sen: The assembly overrules the Senate on its own decree.
reasons.eqt: Exemptions voted into law cost the publicani for good.
reasons.lbr: Forgeries made law by a crowd's vote.

callbacks.title: The Heir Sells His Farms
callbacks.question: Octavian sells his farms to pay the bequest. What will you do?
callbacks.body: You refused Caesar's money to the heir. Now he auctions his own estates to pay 300 sesterces a head. The crowd at the Rostra cheers his name. Your refusal is the talk of the Subura.

answers.text: Deny him Caesar's name: no curiate law
answers.sub: No adoption confirmed; no new Caesar while you rule.

reasons.lbr: No new Caesar rising with his father's name.
reasons.sen: A boy kept from a dynasty pleases the consulars.
reasons.oct: His name and his father denied again.
reasons.plb: The crowd's young Caesar blocked by the consul.
reasons.cpt: Caesar's line slighted by Caesar's own officer.

answers.text: Pay the bequest from the treasury at the Rostra
answers.sub: You outbid him for the crowd with public money.

reasons.plb: Two gifts now, and the consul's is bigger.
reasons.oct: He sells his land and you take the thanks.
reasons.sen: Public silver spent to buy a crowd.
reasons.eqt: The treasury drained in a contest of gifts.

callbacks.title: Liberty Cheered

carrier.name: Publius Sestullius
carrier.role: Junior clerk of the urban praetor

callbacks.question: The theatre cheered Brutus. Will you let him come home to Rome?
callbacks.body: You let Accius's play open Brutus's games. The theatre roared at every line against kings. Now Brutus's friends ask safe conduct for him to return as praetor. Veterans in the Forum say they will meet him at the gate.

answers.text: Grant safe conduct and guard his return
answers.sub: Brutus sits in Rome as praetor, under your protection.

reasons.lbr: Brutus comes home with his office honoured.
reasons.sen: The amnesty proved real; concord looks possible.
reasons.cpt: Caesar's officers watch his killer escorted home.
reasons.oct: His father's murderer guarded by the consul.
reasons.plb: The crowd that burned their houses sees them back.

answers.gripWhy: Rome's gates open to the men of the Ides.

answers.text: Call a contio and let the crowd answer
answers.sub: The plebs shout down Brutus's return at the Rostra.

reasons.plb: The people speak at the Rostra, not a stage.
reasons.cpt: The veterans' voice joins the crowd's.
reasons.lbr: Their cheering theatre drowned by the Forum crowd.
reasons.sen: A crowd, not the Senate, decides a praetor's fate.

callbacks.title: Blood at Brundisium

carrier.name: Quintus Tullius Crispus
carrier.role: Clerk to a tribune of the plebs

callbacks.question: The dead centurions' comrades ask justice. What will you give them?
callbacks.body: At Brundisium you had the named ringleaders executed before the ranks. Their comrades still talk of it at the campfires. Cicero says your wife's dress was spattered with blood. A tribune proposes that soldiers keep the citizen's right of appeal.

answers.text: Restore their right of appeal; no more summary killings.
answers.sub: Soldiers are citizens again before the law, even in camp.

reasons.sen: Citizens tried, not slaughtered: the laws of appeal live.
reasons.plb: The citizen's right of appeal, defended for soldiers too.
reasons.lbr: The consul admits the tyrant's methods were wrong.
reasons.cpt: No commander holds an army without the power to punish.

answers.gripWhy: You give up the commander's power of life and death.

answers.text: Pay their families and settle their sons on land.
answers.sub: Silver to the widows; allotments for the dead men's kin.

reasons.plb: Widows paid and orphans given land: a generous consul.
reasons.cpt: Veterans see the families of the fallen looked after.
reasons.eqt: More land, more silver, and none of it ours to keep.
reasons.sen: Blood money from the public chest, without a decree.
reasons.oct: You buy back soldiers who were turning to me.

callbacks.title: The Unarmed Forum

carrier.name: Marcus Volusius
carrier.role: Attendant of a tribune of the plebs

callbacks.question: With no soldiers in Rome, how will you answer the city?
callbacks.body: You sent your guard out of the city and kept the pomerium free of arms. Now Cicero speaks against you in every session, and no one stops him. The tribunes call daily meetings at the Rostra. Your friends in Rome ask for a voice.

answers.text: Let him speak; answer by open letter.
answers.sub: Your letter is read in the Senate; no one is silenced.

reasons.sen: A proconsul who writes rather than threatens earns a hearing.
reasons.lbr: Free speech honoured, even when it wounds you.
reasons.eqt: Letters, not legions: bankers like a quiet city.
reasons.cpt: Cicero calls us bandits and you send letters.
reasons.plb: The Forum wants a champion, not a letter.

answers.gripWhy: The Senate debates freely, your critics untouched.

answers.text: Have the tribes vote your command in Gaul.
answers.sub: Your friends among the tribunes carry it at the contio.

reasons.plb: The people decide who commands, not the Curia.
reasons.cpt: A law of the people keeps our general's legions lawful.
reasons.sen: The tribes again over the Senate's head, as in June.
reasons.lbr: Decimus's province taken by a plebiscite: tyranny by vote.
reasons.eqt: Another fight over Gaul delays the peace we need.

callbacks.title: Gaius at Apollonia
callbacks.question: Brutus has your brother trapped at Apollonia. What will you do for him?
callbacks.body: You gave Macedonia to your brother Gaius on the night of the allotment. Brutus reached it first. The Macedonian legions went over to him. Gaius is shut up in Apollonia with a handful of cohorts. The Senate has confirmed Brutus as governor.

answers.text: Appeal to Brutus: free citizens do not kill captives
answers.sub: You concede him Macedonia and ask Gaius's life in return.

reasons.lbr: Macedonia is conceded, and Brutus's mercy is praised.
reasons.cpt: You yield a province to an assassin for one man.
reasons.oct: The proconsul bargains with Caesar's murderer.
reasons.sen: The proconsul admits the Senate's governor is lawful.
reasons.par: Brutus secure in Macedonia keeps Rome split in two.

answers.gripWhy: You concede by letter what your legions cannot take.

answers.text: Ask your Senate friends to annul Brutus's command
answers.sub: Your friends argue the Senate's own decree named Gaius.

reasons.sen: We will not undo our own vote for Brutus.
reasons.cpt: Fighting for a Caesarian's province, at least in words.
reasons.lbr: Brutus's lawful command attacked from the Curia.
reasons.eqt: A dispute settled by decree, not by legions in Epirus.
reasons.egy: Macedonia back in Caesarian hands would guard the East.

callbacks.title: The Picene Towns Complain
callbacks.question: Your soldiers took Picene land and goods. Will you give anything back?
callbacks.body: Ventidius's two legions were paid with the farms and stores of towns that shut their gates. Now their councillors stand before the Senate in mourning dress. The equites of Picenum have stopped lending. The Senate cites their case in every speech against you.

answers.text: Return the goods and pardon the towns that resisted
answers.sub: Free towns keep their liberty to shut their gates.

reasons.eqt: Our goods back and the law of property respected.
reasons.lbr: Towns that defied you are pardoned, not punished.
reasons.cpt: Ventidius's men lose what they were promised.
reasons.sen: One crime against citizens undone.
reasons.plb: The rich towns get their stores back; the soldiers pay.

answers.gripWhy: You give back what soldiers seized and pardon defiance.

answers.text: Let the courts assess claims after the war
answers.sub: Owners get a hearing and a bond, not their farms.

reasons.eqt: A bond for later is a debt that may never pay.
reasons.sen: Courts after the war: the proconsul delays justice.
reasons.cpt: The soldiers keep their land while lawyers argue.
reasons.lbr: Plunder made legal by a promise of hearings.
reasons.plb: Legions paid and the city spared new levies.
